newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to exempt Europeso proceeds from tax.
newsitem.headline: Manila to exempt Europeso proceeds from tax.

text.p: The Philippines will exempt proceeds from the offshore issue of peso-denominated instruments called Europeso from domestic taxation, officials said.

The proceeds would be covered instead by taxation regulations in the country of origin of the Europeso investors, officials of the finance department and the bureau of internal revenue told reporters on Saturday
Finance undersecretary Milwida Guevara said whether the issuer was a local or a foreign firm, it was the offshore investors who would generate interest income since the funds would be sourced abroad.
The Philippine Monetary Board last week approved proposals by the World Bank and its investment arm, the International Finance Corp (IFC), to issue Europeso notes.
The World Bank and IFC will separately undertake the maiden sale of the Europeso notes through their respective lead managers, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Citibank.
The issue size will be in the range of 2.5 to 4.0 billion pesos for each institution, the Central Bank said.
The Europeso issues are expected to have a maturity of up to five years and an interest rate below government securities of comparable maturities, a Central Bank official said.
